theory.title: Components in React
theory.content:
Functional Components

Modern approach — regular functions returning JSX:

function Button({ label, onClick }) {
  return ;
}

Class Components

Older approach, still used:

class Button extends React.Component {
  render() {
    return ;
  }
}

Props

Way to pass data into a component:

const Greeting = ({ name }) => 
Hello, {name}!
;

theory.title: State and Hooks
theory.content:
useState — Manage State

function Counter() {
  const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
  return (
    

      
Count: {count}

      
    

  );
}

useEffect — Side Effects

Executes code on mount, update, or unmount:

useEffect(() => {
  const timer = setInterval(() => {
    console.log('tick');
  }, 1000);

  return () => clearInterval(timer); // cleanup
}, []); // dependencies

Other Main Hooks

  • useContext — access context
  • useReducer — complex state
  • useRef — direct DOM reference

theory.title: Component Lifecycle
theory.content:
In Functional Components

Lifecycle implemented via useEffect:

// Mounting (first render)
useEffect(() => {
  console.log('Component mounted');
}, []);

// Updating (any changes)
useEffect(() => {
  console.log('Component updated');
});

// Unmounting
useEffect(() => {
  return () => console.log('Component unmounted');
}, []);

In Class Components

  • componentDidMount — after mount
  • componentDidUpdate — after update
  • componentWillUnmount — before unmount

theory.title: Component Optimization
theory.content:
React.memo

Prevents re-render when props don't change:

const Button = React.memo(({ label, onClick }) => {
  return ;
});

useMemo and useCallback

Cache results for optimization:

const memoized = useMemo(() => expensiveComputation(value), [value]);
const memoCallback = useCallback(() => handleClick(), []);

theory.title: API Integration
theory.content:
Loading Data with Fetch

useEffect(() => {
  fetch('/api/data')
    .then(res => res.json())
    .then(data => setData(data))
    .catch(err => setError(err));
}, []);

Error Handling

Use state to store errors and display to user
